title: Kerala Police MoU With Cyble For Threat Intelligence
summary: Kerala Police signs a MoU with Cyble to strengthen cybercrime investigations through threat intelligence, officer training, and threat research.

# Kerala Police Signs MoU with Cyble to Tap Threat Intelligence for Cybercrime Probes


*Partnership will strengthen cybercrime investigations through AI-powered threat intelligence, specialized officer training, and research into emerging cyber threats under a three-year MoU.*


**THIRUVANANTHAPURAM, India, October 12, 2026** — Cyble, an AI-native cybersecurity company, has signed a three-year Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Kerala Police to strengthen cybercrime investigations through[threat intelligence](https://cyble.com/solutions/cyber-threat-intelligence/) , investigative support, and capacity building. The agreement, signed through Cyble’s Indian subsidiary, Cyble Infosec India Private Limited, will support the Kerala Police Cyber Operations wing and Cyberdome in identifying and investigating emerging cyber threats.


Cybercriminals increasingly use underground online forums and illicit marketplaces to trade stolen credentials, distribute leaked data, coordinate ransomware operations, and facilitate fraud. Identifying these activities before they cause harm requires timely intelligence and effective collaboration between technology providers and law enforcement agencies.


Through this MoU, Cyble will support Kerala Police with intelligence relevant to cybercrime investigations, including compromised credentials, ransomware activity, data leaks, phishing and fraud infrastructure, and the impersonation of government and police brands. The collaboration also includes no-cost evaluation access to select Cyble platforms, training for police officers in open-source intelligence (OSINT) and[dark web investigations](https://cyble.com/blog/dark-web-intelligence-monitoring-guide/) , and joint research into emerging threats such as AI-enabled fraud, deepfakes, mule account networks, and investment scams. Public awareness initiatives will also form part of the collaboration.


“Effective cybercrime investigations require timely intelligence, especially when criminal activity originates across borders and moves through hidden online networks,” said Beenu Arora, Co-Founder and CEO of Cyble. “Kerala Police has taken a proactive approach to cyber policing through Cyberdome. Through this collaboration, we aim to help investigators access relevant threat intelligence, strengthen their investigative capabilities, and better understand emerging threats targeting citizens and institutions.”


“Cybercrime investigations increasingly require access to timely intelligence on threats that may originate beyond conventional online channels. This collaboration will support Cyberdome and our officers with relevant intelligence, strengthen investigative capabilities, and contribute to efforts to protect citizens from evolving cyber threats,” said Ankit Asokan, IPS, Kerala Police.


The MoU reflects a shared focus on strengthening cybercrime response through collaboration, intelligence sharing, and knowledge development. By combining Cyble’s threat intelligence capabilities with Kerala Police’s investigative expertise, the partnership aims to support more informed investigations and improve awareness of emerging cyber risks.


### About Cyble


Cyble is an AI-native cybersecurity company helping governments and enterprises identify, prioritize, and respond to cyber threats. Its portfolio includes Cyble Vision, Blaze AI, and Cyble Titan, supporting capabilities across threat intelligence, dark web monitoring, attack surface management, brand protection, and endpoint security. Headquartered in Cupertino, California, Cyble serves customers globally, with offices across regions including Australia, Malaysia, Singapore, the Middle East, and India.
